threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, sectors, and case types for the standardisation project.

messages.text: Good morning team. We're kicking off the Cross-Sector Digital Intake and Case-Handling Standardisation project today. The goal is to design and pilot a unified workflow across health, education, courts and civil service within 30 days. Before we dive into the detailed work, we need to align on scope: which case types per sector should we prioritise in this first wave? We'll be documenting current workflows in A1 and using T1, T2, T3, T4 to map out what each sector is doing now. Please share your thoughts on what's realistic to cover.

Thanks for the kickoff. From education, we handle student intake, enrolment queries, and transfer requests. I'd suggest we focus on student intake first—it's the highest volume and will give us good feedback. For the timeline, I think we should aim to have the data model ready by day 10 so we can design forms in parallel. Does that sound feasible?

Medical side: we process patient intake, referrals, and consent forms. Patient intake is definitely the core—that's where most errors happen. I'll need to document the current process in T1, but I want to flag that we have some legacy forms that don't capture all the data we need. Should we be thinking about that when we design the new templates?

Court perspective: we manage case registration, evidence intake, and scheduling. Standard civil cases are our main volume. I'll map the current process in T3, but I need to be clear—any new workflow must respect the civil process order and legal time limits. Those are non-negotiable. I can validate the court form design once we have a draft.

Agreed on the legal constraints. I'll support the T3 documentation and can help review the court form later. One question: are we including evidence handling in the intake form, or is that a separate process?
Good question. Evidence intake is part of the registration step, so it should be in the form. We'll need to be explicit about what documents are mandatory and what the deadlines are.

Civil service: we handle public enquiries, complaints, and information requests. I'd propose we start with information requests—they're high volume and relatively straightforward. I'll document the current process in T4. On timeline: day 10 for the data model works. We should also confirm milestones for the SOP (day 20?) and pilot start (day 25?). Does that align with everyone's capacity?

Day 20 for SOP and day 25 for pilot start sounds tight but doable. I'll need to coordinate with the team on the data model review—that's critical path. Should we schedule a weekly sync to track progress, or are async updates enough?

Let's do twice-weekly async check-ins where each of you posts progress on your assigned tasks and any blockers. That way we stay aligned without too many meetings. I'll set up a template for that. So to confirm scope: education (student intake), medical (patient intake), court (civil case registration with evidence), civil service (information requests). All agreed?
Agreed on medical patient intake. I'll start documenting T1 today.
Court side is good with civil case registration. I'll begin T3 mapping.
Education confirmed. Starting T2 now.

Perfect. I'll document civil service information requests in T4 and set up the tracking sheet. Timeline confirmed: data model by day 10, SOP by day 20, pilot start day 25. Let's reconvene in the weekly review thread once we have the current-state maps ready.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise the unified intake data model and standard forms.

messages.text: Team, I've drafted the unified intake data model in A2 based on the current-state maps from T1, T2, T3, T4. The model identifies common fields (name, contact, case type, date received) and sector-specific mandatory fields (e.g., medical consent, court evidence list, education enrolment status). I've also started sketching the medical intake form in T6 and court form in T7. Please review A2 and let me know if I've missed anything critical or if the field definitions need adjustment.

Thanks for pulling this together. Looking at A2, I see the common fields are solid. For medical, I notice the consent field is there, but we also need to capture insurance type and patient ID. Those are mandatory in our system. Should I add those to the sector-specific section, or are they already covered?

Good catch. Insurance type and patient ID should go in the medical-specific section. I'll update A2 to include those. Court, can you review the mandatory fields for case registration? I want to make sure I haven't missed any legal requirements.

I've reviewed A2. The court-specific fields look correct: case type, parties involved, evidence list, and legal deadline. However, I need to flag that the evidence list structure needs to be very clear—we need to know what documents are attached, their dates, and who submitted them. This is critical for the civil process order. Can you add a sub-section for that in the form design?
Understood. I'll add a structured evidence tracking section to T7. That will help ensure nothing gets lost. Civil service, any feedback on the common fields or the information request fields?

The common fields work well for civil service. I'd add one more: 'enquiry category' so we can route requests properly. Also, I want to make sure the data model is clear on what's optional vs. mandatory—that will help with form design and staff training. Can you add a column in A2 marking that?

Good idea. I'll add a 'mandatory' column to A2 and include the enquiry category field. Let me revise and share the updated version by EOD tomorrow. Once that's approved, I can finalise T6 and T7 with the sector-specific forms.
I'll test the medical form draft in T6 with a sample patient intake case once you've updated it. That way we can catch any usability issues early.
I'll do the same for the court form in T7. I'll test it against a standard civil case and make sure the evidence section works as intended.

Perfect. Once you've both tested and I've incorporated feedback, we'll have the forms ready for sign-off. I'll schedule a review thread for day 12 to get final approval on A2 and the form templates before we move to the SOP.
Sounds good. Once the forms are approved, we can move forward with the SOP design. I'll be ready to coordinate that next phase.
Great. Updated A2 is ready for review. All: please confirm the data model and field definitions by EOD day 11 so we can lock it in and move to form finalisation.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on confidentiality rules and how they apply in the new workflow.

messages.text: I've drafted the cross-sector confidentiality and data handling guideline in A3 based on the requirements from each sector. The guideline covers access control, document sharing, retention, and breach reporting. It's designed to align with medical privacy rules, court confidentiality orders, education data protection, and civil service transparency requirements. Please review and flag any gaps or conflicts with your sector's rules.

I've reviewed A3. The access control section is solid, but I need to highlight a court-specific requirement: sealed documents and evidence must be restricted to authorised court staff only. The guideline mentions 'case team access', but we need to be explicit that this excludes public access and requires judicial approval for any disclosure. Can you add that?
Absolutely. I'll add a court-specific section on sealed documents and judicial approval requirements. Medical side: are there similar restrictions on patient data access?

Yes. Patient data is restricted to clinical and administrative staff directly involved in the case. We also need explicit rules on consent—patients must opt in for any data sharing beyond direct care. That's a legal requirement. I'd suggest adding a consent tracking section to A3.

Got it. I'll add medical consent tracking and court judicial approval sections. Civil service has different rules—information requests are generally public unless they contain personal data. I'll add a section on that too. Let me revise A3 and share by EOD tomorrow.
I'll review the updated A3 once it's ready. Education data is also sensitive—we need to protect student records and ensure parental consent where required. I'll flag any gaps when I see the revision.
Thanks. I'll include education consent and parental notification rules in the revision. Once all sectors have reviewed and confirmed, we can sign off on A3 and incorporate it into the SOP.
Agreed. I'll review the updated version and confirm court requirements are met.
Updated A3 is ready. All: please confirm by EOD day 13 so we can lock in the confidentiality rules and move to SOP design.

threads.thread_goal: Validate the unified intake workflow, SOP, and frontline checklists.

messages.text: I've drafted the unified intake workflow and SOP in A4 based on the approved data model, forms, and confidentiality guideline. The SOP covers the end-to-end process for all sectors: intake, data entry, validation, confidentiality checks, and case routing. I've also prepared draft quick-reference checklists in A5 for frontline staff. Please test both with sample cases from your sector and let me know if the workflow is clear and complete.

I've tested A4 with a sample patient intake case. The workflow is mostly clear, but I found a gap: the SOP doesn't specify who verifies the consent form before the case is registered. In medical, that's a critical step. Can you add that to the validation section?
Good catch. I'll add a consent verification step to the validation section and assign it to the medical intake officer. I'll also update A5 to include that in the medical checklist.

I tested A4 with a civil case registration. The workflow covers the main steps, but the evidence validation section needs more detail. We need to specify: what documents are mandatory, what the deadline is for evidence submission, and who approves the evidence list. Can you expand that?
Understood. I'll add a detailed evidence validation sub-section with mandatory documents, deadlines, and approval authority. I'll also update the court checklist in A5 to reflect that.

I tested A4 with an information request case. The workflow is solid for civil service. One suggestion: the routing step could be clearer about which enquiry categories go to which department. I'll add that detail to the civil service checklist in A5.
Good idea. I'll add a routing matrix to A4 and reference it in the civil service checklist. That will make it easier for staff to know where to send each request.

I reviewed A4 from a court perspective as well. The steps are logical, but I want to confirm: does the SOP include a step for notifying parties of case registration? That's a legal requirement in civil cases.
Good point. I'll add a notification step after case registration. That should be assigned to the court administrative officer. I'll update A4 and the court checklist.

I've incorporated all the feedback. Updated A4 now includes: consent verification for medical, detailed evidence validation for court, notification step for court, and routing matrix for civil service. A5 checklists have been updated to match. Please review the revised versions and confirm they're ready for pilot use.
Reviewed. The medical sections look good now. I'm ready to sign off on A4 and A5 for medical.
Court sections are solid. The evidence validation and notification steps are now clear. I'm ready to sign off.
Civil service sections are good. The routing matrix is helpful. I'm ready to sign off on A4 and A5.
Excellent. All sectors have confirmed. A4 and A5 are now approved for pilot implementation. We're on track for the day 20 SOP deadline and day 25 pilot start.

threads.thread_goal: Plan the pilot, track issues, and agree on improvement actions.

messages.text: We're ready to launch the pilot on day 25. I've prepared the pilot tracking sheet in A6 to capture cases, issues, and feedback from all sectors. The pilot will run for 5 days (day 25-29) with a focus on the case types we agreed: medical patient intake, court civil case registration, education student intake, and civil service information requests. Each sector will process 5-10 cases using the new workflow and forms. I'll consolidate feedback daily and we'll meet on day 30 to review results and plan improvements. Any questions on scope or tracking approach?
Pilot scope is clear. I'll process 5-10 patient intake cases and log any issues in A6. One question: should I also track time spent on each case? That would help us measure efficiency improvements.
Good idea. I'll add a 'time spent' column to A6. That will help us measure processing time improvements. Please log the time for each case.
Court pilot is ready. I'll process 5-10 civil case registrations and track any issues with the evidence validation or notification steps. Should I also note any legal compliance issues?
Absolutely. Please flag any legal compliance issues immediately—those are critical. I'll add a 'compliance' column to A6 so we can track those separately.
Education is ready. I'll process student intake cases and track issues. One concern: I want to make sure the form is easy enough for our intake staff to use. Should I also note usability feedback?
Yes, usability feedback is important. I'll add a 'usability' column to A6. That will help us refine the forms and checklists before full rollout.
I'll support the court pilot and help track issues. Should we also note any training gaps—things that staff struggled with because they didn't understand the new process?
Good point. I'll add a 'training gap' column to A6. That will help us identify what needs to be clarified in the training materials before full rollout.

Updated A6 is ready with columns for: case ID, sector, case type, time spent, issues, compliance, usability, and training gaps. I'll send daily summaries to the team during the pilot. On day 30, I'll consolidate all feedback into the pilot evaluation report in A7 with improvement recommendations. Does everyone agree on this approach?
Agreed. I'm ready to start the pilot on day 25.
Ready. I'll begin court case processing on day 25.
Education is ready. Starting day 25.
Perfect. Pilot starts day 25. I'll send daily summaries and we'll reconvene on day 30 to review results and plan next steps. T11 and T12 are now in motion.

Day 25 pilot summary: All sectors have begun processing cases. Medical has completed 3 patient intakes with no major issues. Court has processed 2 civil cases—one compliance note on evidence deadline tracking. Education has completed 4 student intakes with positive usability feedback. Civil service has processed 3 information requests smoothly. I'll continue daily updates.

Day 26 court update: Processed 3 more civil cases. Found one issue: the evidence deadline field in the form is confusing—staff weren't sure if it was the submission deadline or the court deadline. We need to clarify that in the form or training.
Day 26 medical update: Completed 4 more patient intakes. All cases processed smoothly. Consent verification step is working well. No issues to report.

Day 26 education update: Completed 3 more student intakes. Staff found the routing section helpful. One minor usability note: the form could benefit from clearer field labels for non-native English speakers. I'll note that for improvement.
Thanks for the updates. I'm tracking all issues in A6. The evidence deadline confusion and field label clarity are both noted. I'll consolidate all feedback on day 30 and propose improvements in A7.

Day 30 pilot summary: All sectors completed their cases. Total: 25 cases processed across all sectors. Key findings: 1) Evidence deadline field needs clarification (court). 2) Field labels need simplification for accessibility (education). 3) Consent verification working well (medical). 4) Routing matrix effective (civil service). I'm finalising A7 with detailed recommendations. We'll review on day 30 and plan next steps.
